# Overview



SCimilarity is a foundation model for single-cell biology that provides a **unifying representation of single cell expression profiles**, enabling researchers to quantify similarity between cell states across studies without requiring additional training or specialized preprocessing [docs/index.rst#L11-L13](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/index.rst#L11-L13). The framework enables a novel cell search capability that can sift through millions of profiles to find cells similar to a query cell state, allowing researchers to systematically leverage massive public scRNA-seq atlases [README.rst#L5-L10](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/README.rst#L5-L10).

![Search Engine Overview](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/search_engine.png?raw=true)

The framework's core innovation lies in its ability to generalize across studies using a pre-trained neural network architecture that learns meaningful latent representations of cellular expression profiles. This eliminates the need for batch correction, highly variable gene selection, or other complex preprocessing steps typically required in comparative single-cell analysis [docs/index.rst#L28-L30](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/index.rst#L28-L30).

Sources: [README.rst](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/README.rst#L1-L43), [docs/index.rst](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/index.rst#L1-L85), [src/scimilarity/__init__.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/__init__.py#L1-L23)

## Architecture

SCimilarity's architecture follows a modular design pattern centered around four core capabilities: cell embedding generation, similarity search, cell type annotation, and interpretability analysis. The system supports multiple data storage backends (AnnData, TileDB, Zarr) and provides both pre-trained models and training utilities for custom model development [src/scimilarity/__init__.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/__init__.py#L18-L23).

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Layer"
        %% 定义输入节点
        A[Single Cell Data] 
        B[AnnData Data Model]
        C[TileDB Data Model]
        D[Zarr Data Model]
        
        %% 输入层内部连接
        A --> B
        A --> C
        A --> D
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Processing"
        %% 定义核心处理节点
        %% 注意：这里使用了与原代码不同的 ID (E, F, G) 以确保定义的唯一性
        E[CellEmbedding Module]
        F[Encoder-Decoder Neural Network]
        G[Latent Space Representation]
        
        %% 核心层内部连接
        E --> F
        F --> G
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis Layer"
        %% 定义分析层节点
        H[CellQuery - Similarity Search]
        I[CellAnnotation - Classification]
        J[Interpreter - Gene Attribution]
    end
    
    subgraph "Training Layer"
        %% 定义训练层节点
        K[MetricLearning Module]
        L[Triplet Loss Training]
        M[PyTorch Lightning Integration]
        
        %% 训练层内部连接
        K --> L
        L --> M
    end
    
    %% === 跨层连接 ===
    
    %% Input Layer -> Core Processing
    B --> E
    C --> E
    D --> E
    
    %% Core Processing -> Analysis Layer
    %% 注：原代码中有 H --> G 和 I --> G，这会导致循环引用或逻辑冲突，通常架构图流向是单向的，因此移除了反向连接。
    G --> H
    G --> I
    G --> J
```

The foundation of this architecture is the **CellEmbedding** class, which loads pre-trained encoder-decoder neural network models and transforms gene expression profiles into 128-dimensional latent space vectors [src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py#L19-L24](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py#L19-L24). This embedding generation capability serves as the foundation for both search and annotation functionality, with the neural network having been trained on diverse single-cell datasets to create a universal representation space [src/scimilarity/nn_models.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/nn_models.py).

Building upon the embedding layer, the framework provides specialized analysis modules. The **CellQuery** class enables similarity search across millions of pre-computed cell embeddings using efficient K-Nearest Neighbors algorithms (HNSW) [src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L31-L40](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L31-L40), while **CellAnnotation** leverages the same K-NN infrastructure to classify cell types by finding the most similar cells in a reference catalog of 7 million author-annotated cells [docs/index.rst#L45-L52](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/index.rst#L45-L52).

Sources: [src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py#L1-L157), [src/scimilarity/cell_query.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L1-L744), [src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L1-L320)

## Core Capabilities

SCimilarity provides three primary capabilities that address common challenges in single-cell analysis workflows:

| Capability | Primary Module | Key Features | Use Case |
|------------|----------------|--------------|----------|
| **Similarity Search** | CellQuery | HNSW K-NN, exhaustive search, metadata filtering | Find cells matching a query profile across millions of references |
| **Cell Type Classification** | CellAnnotation | Reference catalog of 7M cells, safelist/blocklist, prediction weighting | Annotate new datasets without user-provided references |
| **Interpretability** | Interpreter | Gene attribution, ranked gene comparison, visualization | Understand which genes drive similarity/differences between cell states |

### Cell Query

The **CellQuery** module provides tools to search for similar cells across large reference datasets. Users input a gene expression profile of a cell state of interest, and the system searches across tens of millions of cells to find cells that resemble the query cell state [docs/index.rst#L28-L36](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/index.rst#L28-L36). This capability requires no special preprocessing such as batch correction or highly variable gene selection, making it accessible to researchers regardless of their bioinformatics expertise.

![Cell Query Model](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/query_model.png?raw=true)

The module supports multiple search strategies including fast approximate K-NN search using HNSWlib (`search_nearest`, `search_centroid_nearest`) and exhaustive search with distance thresholds (`search_exhaustive`, `search_centroid_exhaustive`) [src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L206-L287](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L206-L287). Users can also filter results based on metadata criteria such as tissue type, disease state, or study origin [src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L479](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L479).

### Cell Type Annotation

The **CellAnnotation** class classifies cells by finding the most similar cells in a reference catalog of 7 million author-annotated cells [docs/index.rst#L45-L52](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/index.rst#L45-L52). This eliminates the need for users to provide their own reference datasets, though users can subset the reference to cell types of interest to increase annotation accuracy. The module provides sophisticated cell type management through safelist and blocklist functionality, allowing researchers to control which cell types are considered during classification [src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L92-L119](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L92-L119).

![Annotation Model](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/annotation_model.png?raw=true)

> [!TIP]
> The annotation process leverages prediction weighting strategies that can be enabled or disabled depending on use case requirements, providing flexibility between simple majority voting and weighted similarity-based classification.

### Model Training

For researchers requiring custom models, the **MetricLearning** class provides comprehensive functionality to train new SCimilarity models using PyTorch Lightning [src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L15-L16](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L15-L16). The training framework implements metric learning with triplet loss, enabling the model to learn meaningful representations where similar cell types cluster together and dissimilar types are separated in latent space [src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L73-L93](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L73-L93).

![Model Training](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/model_training.png?raw=true)

Key training features include configurable triplet selection strategies (semihard, random), study-aware sampling, label perturbation for robustness, and comprehensive tracking of training metrics through the PyTorch Lightning callback system [src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L82-L85](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L82-L85). The framework supports both encoder-only and encoder-decoder architectures with customizable hidden layer dimensions and dropout rates [src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L76-L79](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L76-L79).

Sources: [docs/index.rst](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/index.rst#L28-L78), [src/scimilarity/cell_query.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L31-L287), [src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L23-L156), [src/scimilarity/training_models.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/training_models.py#L73-L93)

## Data Model Architecture

SCimilarity provides flexible data model support to accommodate different research workflows and data storage requirements:

| Data Model | Primary Classes | Storage Backend | Typical Use Case |
|------------|-----------------|-----------------|------------------|
| **AnnData** | scDataset, MetricLearningDataModule | HDF5 (AnnData format) | Training models, moderate-sized datasets |
| **TileDB** | scDataset, scSampler, MetricLearningDataModule | TileDB arrays | Large-scale production deployments, cloud storage |
| **Zarr** | scDataset, scSampler, MetricLearningDataModule | Zarr arrays | Distributed computing, chunked access patterns |

The **AnnData data models** provide a familiar interface for researchers working with the AnnData ecosystem, supporting direct integration with existing single-cell analysis pipelines [src/scimilarity/anndata_data_models.py#L20-L30](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/anndata_data_models.py#L20-L30). For larger-scale deployments, the **TileDB data models** offer optimized storage and sampling strategies with dynamic weight decay for training efficiency [src/scimilarity/tiledb_data_models.py#L48-L77](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/tiledb_data_models.py#L48-L77). The Zarr data models provide similar capabilities with compatibility for cloud-native workflows [src/scimilarity/zarr_data_models.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/zarr_data_models.py).

All data models share a common interface through the PyTorch Lightning DataModule architecture, enabling seamless switching between storage backends without changing training or analysis code. This design allows researchers to prototype with smaller AnnData files and scale to TileDB or Zarr for production workloads without major code refactoring [src/scimilarity/anndata_data_models.py#L70-L80](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/anndata_data_models.py#L70-L80).

## Interpretability and Analysis

The **Interpreter** module provides tools to understand which genes drive similarity between cell states, offering critical insights into biological mechanisms underlying observed relationships [src/scimilarity/interpreter.py#L43-L63](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/interpreter.py#L43-L63). By computing gene attributions through gradient-based methods, researchers can identify the most important genes distinguishing similar or dissimilar cell states, facilitating hypothesis generation and biological interpretation of search results.

The interpreter provides ranked gene lists that can be visualized directly, enabling rapid assessment of the molecular signatures associated with particular cell states or similarity relationships [src/scimilarity/interpreter.py#L133-L171](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/interpreter.py#L133-L171). This capability is particularly valuable for validating search results, understanding why certain cell types cluster together, and generating novel hypotheses about cellular relationships.

> [!TIP]
> Gene attribution calculations leverage the SimpleDist neural network module, which computes distances between cell representations while maintaining differentiability to enable gradient-based feature importance estimation.

Sources: [src/scimilarity/interpreter.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/interpreter.py#L5-L171), [src/scimilarity/anndata_data_models.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/anndata_data_models.py#L1-L375), [src/scimilarity/tiledb_data_models.py](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/src/scimilarity/tiledb_data_models.py#L1-L686)

## Project Structure

The SCimilarity repository follows a clear, modular structure designed to separate concerns and facilitate maintainability:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Source Code"
        A1[cell_embedding.py] --> B1[Embedding Generation]
        A2[cell_query.py] --> B2[Similarity Search]
        A3[cell_annotation.py] --> B3[Cell Classification]
        A4[training_models.py] --> B4[Model Training]
        A5[interpreter.py] --> B5[Interpretability]
        A6[nn_models.py] --> B6[Neural Architectures]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Models"
        C1[anndata_data_models.py]
        C2[tiledb_data_models.py]
        C3[zarr_data_models.py]
    end
    
    subgraph "Supporting Modules"
        D1[ontologies.py]
        D2[utils.py]
        D3[visualizations.py]
        D4[triplet_selector.py]
    end
    
    subgraph "Documentation"
        E1[Tutorials]
        E2[API Reference]
        E3[Guides]
    end
    
    subgraph "Scripts"
        F1[Training Scripts]
        F2[Build Scripts]
    end
    
    B1 --> C1
    B1 --> C2
    B1 --> C3
    B2 --> B1
    B3 --> B1
    B4 --> C1
    B4 --> D4
    B5 --> A6
    D1 --> C1
    D2 --> B1
```

The source code is organized into logical groupings in the `src/scimilarity/` directory, with core functionality (embedding, query, annotation, training) separated from data model implementations and supporting utilities. The `docs/` directory contains comprehensive tutorials, API documentation, and conceptual guides [docs/tutorials.rst#L1-L14](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/tutorials.rst#L1-L14). The `scripts/` directory provides production-ready scripts for common workflows including model training, embedding generation, and K-NN graph building.

## Getting Started with SCimilarity

To begin using SCimilarity, you have several learning paths depending on your goals and experience level:

- **If you're new to the framework**: Start with [Quick Start](2-quick-start) for a hands-on introduction to basic functionality
- **If you need to set up your environment**: Visit [Installation and Setup](3-installation-and-setup) for detailed installation instructions
- **If you want to start analyzing data immediately**: Check out [Downloading Pretrained Models and Data](4-downloading-pretrained-models-and-data) to access pre-trained models and reference datasets
- **If you prefer containerized environments**: See [Docker Usage](5-docker-usage) for pre-configured container images

For users ready to dive into specific capabilities:

- **Learn about cell search**: Begin with [Cell Embedding Fundamentals](6-cell-embedding-fundamentals) to understand the underlying representation space, then proceed to [Cell Query API Reference](9-cell-query-api-reference)
- **Annotate your datasets**: Start with [Cell Annotation API Reference](13-cell-annotation-api-reference) and [Understanding Cell Type Classification](14-understanding-cell-type-classification)
- **Train custom models**: Review [Metric Learning with Triplet Loss](18-metric-learning-with-triplet-loss) and [Training Configuration and Hyperparameters](20-training-configuration-and-hyperparameters)

The framework provides comprehensive tutorials covering individual cell search, gene signature-based search, cluster-based analysis, cell type annotation, advanced interpretability, and model training workflows [docs/tutorials.rst#L1-L14](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/tutorials.rst#L1-L14).


# Quick Start



Welcome to SCimilarity—a foundation model for single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data that enables scalable cell search and annotation across millions of cells. This Quick Start guide will get you up and running with SCimilarity's core capabilities in under 15 minutes, regardless of your single-cell analysis experience.

SCimilarity provides a unified representation of cell states that generalizes across studies, allowing you to search massive public atlases to find similar cells, annotate unknown cell types, and understand the genetic drivers of cell differences. The library is built on a PyTorch Lightning architecture trained with triplet loss learning, featuring pre-trained models on 23.4 million human cells [README.rst](README.rst#L1-L15).

## Architecture Overview

SCimilarity follows a modular design that separates concerns across embedding generation, search/query operations, annotation, and interpretability. This architecture enables flexible workflows while maintaining performance at scale.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Data Layer"
        A[AnnData/Scanpy Dataset]
        B[Raw Count Matrix]
    end
    
    subgraph "Preprocessing Layer"
        C[align_dataset<br/>Match gene ordering]
        D[lognorm_counts<br/>Normalize to tp10k]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core API Layer"
        E[CellEmbedding<br/>Generate latent representations]
        F[CellQuery<br/>Search across millions of cells]
        G[CellAnnotation<br/>Classify cell types]
        H[Interpreter<br/>Gene attribution analysis]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model & Data Layer"
        I[Pre-trained Encoder Model]
        J[Pre-computed Embeddings<br/>23.4M cells]
        K[HNSW Index<br/>Fast k-NN search]
        L[Metadata Database<br/>Study/Sample/Tissue/Disease]
    end
    
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    E --> G
    F --> J
    F --> K
    F --> L
    G --> J
    G --> K
    E --> H
    H --> I
    
    style E fill:#e1f5ff
    style F fill:#fff4e1
    style G fill:#e8f5e9
    style H fill:#f3e5f5
```

## Installation and Setup

SCimilarity can be installed via pip in minutes, but requires careful attention to system resources. The library operates with high memory requirements due to the scale of its pre-computed indices and embeddings.

![SCimilarity Architecture](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/search_engine.png?raw=true)

### System Requirements

| Component | Minimum Requirement | Recommended | Notes |
|-----------|---------------------|-------------|-------|
| **RAM** | 64 GB | 128 GB+ | Required for loading k-NN indices and metadata |
| **Storage** | 50 GB | 200 GB+ | For model files, embeddings, and datasets |
| **GPU** | Not required | NVIDIA GPU with CUDA | Only needed for model training, not inference |
| **Python** | 3.8 | 3.10+ | Tested on Python 3.10 |

> [!TIP]
> If your environment crashes during model loading or k-NN queries despite having sufficient RAM, this typically indicates outdated dependencies (especially `hnswlib` or `numpy`). Use the Docker container or Conda environment specified below to avoid dependency conflicts.

### Installation Methods

**Option 1: PyPI (Recommended for production)**
```bash
pip install scimilarity
```
Sources: [README.rst](README.rst#L26-L27)

**Option 2: Development Installation**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/genentech/scimilarity.git
cd scimilarity
pip install -e .
```
Sources: [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L15-L21)

**Option 3: Docker Container**
```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/genentech/scimilarity:latest
```
The Docker container includes four preset bind points: `/models`, `/data`, `/workspace`, and `/scratch`. For development work:
```bash
docker run -it --platform linux/amd64 -p 8888:8888 \
    -v /path/to/workspace:/workspace \
    -v /path/to/data:/data \
    -v /path/to/models:/models \
    ghcr.io/genentech/scimilarity:latest start-notebook
```
Sources: [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L53-L78)

### Download Pre-trained Models and Data

SCimilarity requires pre-trained model weights, embeddings, k-NN indices, and metadata for full functionality. These assets are distributed via Zenodo:

```bash
# Download model files (~10GB compressed)
curl -L -o /models/model_v1.1.tar.gz \
  https://zenodo.org/records/10685499/files/model_v1.1.tar.gz?download=1
tar -xzvf /models/model_v1.1.tar.gz
```

The model archive contains:
- **Encoder model** (`encoder.ckpt`): Neural network for generating embeddings
- **Gene order** (`gene_order.tsv`): Fixed ordering of 23,469 genes
- **Layer configuration** (`layer_sizes.json`): Network architecture parameters
- **Label mappings** (`label_ints.csv`): Cell ontology label encodings

After installation and model download, you can proceed to SCimilarity's three core workflows. For detailed installation troubleshooting, see [Installation and Setup](3-installation-and-setup). For a complete breakdown of downloadable assets, visit [Downloading Pretrained Models and Data](4-downloading-pretrained-models-and-data).

## Core Workflow: Data Preprocessing

Before using any SCimilarity API, your data must be preprocessed to match the format used during model training. This ensures accurate embeddings and reliable search results.

![Cell Search Workflow](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/search_thumbnail_1.png?raw=true)

### Step 1: Load Your Data

SCimilarity works seamlessly with AnnData objects from the Scanpy ecosystem:

```python
import scanpy as sc
from scimilarity.utils import align_dataset, lognorm_counts

# Load your scRNA-seq dataset
adata = sc.read("path/to/your/data.h5ad")
```

### Step 2: Align Gene Space

SCimilarity uses a fixed gene ordering across all datasets. The `align_dataset` function reorders your data's gene space and handles missing genes:

```python
from scimilarity import CellQuery

# Initialize any SCimilarity API object to access gene_order
cq = CellQuery(model_path="/models/model_v1.1")

# Align dataset to SCimilarity's gene ordering
adata = align_dataset(adata, cq.gene_order)
```

This function performs three critical operations:
1. **Reorders genes** to match the training data's fixed ordering
2. **Zero-fills missing genes** that exist in SCimilarity but not your dataset
3. **Validates compatibility** (requires ≥5,000 overlapping genes)

The model was trained with high data dropout, making it robust to differences in gene lists between datasets [docs/notebooks/cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb](docs/notebooks/cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb#L133-L137).
Sources: [src/scimilarity/utils.py](src/scimilarity/utils.py#L58-L94)

### Step 3: Normalize Expression

SCimilarity expects log-normalized counts targeting 10,000 transcripts per cell:

```python
adata = lognorm_counts(adata)
```

The `lognorm_counts` function performs:
1. **Count normalization**: Scales counts to sum to 10,000 per cell
2. **Log transformation**: Applies log1p transformation
3. **NAN handling**: Converts any NaN values to zeros

**Critical requirement**: Your raw counts must be stored in `adata.layers["counts"]` before normalization.
Sources: [src/scimilarity/utils.py](src/scimilarity/utils.py#L8-L50)

Once preprocessed, your data is ready for any SCimilarity workflow. For deeper understanding of the embedding process, see [Cell Embedding Fundamentals](6-cell-embedding-fundamentals).

## Workflow 1: Cell Search (Finding Similar Cells)

The most common SCimilarity use case is searching for similar cells across millions of profiles. This enables you to leverage public atlases to understand cell states of interest.

### Quick Example: Search IPF-derived Myofibroblasts

```python
from scimilarity import CellQuery

# Initialize CellQuery (loads model and pre-computed indices)
model_path = "/models/model_v1.1"
cq = CellQuery(model_path=model_path)

# Preprocess your data (as shown above)
adata = align_dataset(adata, cq.gene_order)
adata = lognorm_counts(adata)

# Generate embeddings for your query cells
adata.obsm["X_scimilarity"] = cq.get_embeddings(adata.X)

# Search for similar cells across the 23.4M cell atlas
nn_idxs, nn_dists, metadata = cq.search_nearest(
    embeddings=adata.obsm["X_scimilarity"],
    k=100,  # Return top 100 nearest neighbors per query cell
)

# Analyze results: compile sample metadata from matches
results = cq.compile_sample_metadata(
    nn_idxs,
    levels=["study", "sample", "tissue", "disease"]
)
print(results.head())
```

### Understanding the Output

The `search_nearest` method returns three components:

| Output | Description | Shape |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| `nn_idxs` | Indices of nearest neighbors in the pre-computed database | List of arrays, one per query cell |
| `nn_dists` | Euclidean distances to each neighbor | List of arrays, same shape as `nn_idxs` |
| `metadata` | Full metadata for all matched cells | DataFrame with columns: study_id, sample_id, cell_id, tissue, disease, cell_type |

The `compile_sample_metadata` function aggregates information from matches to show which studies, samples, tissues, and diseases contain cells similar to your query. This is particularly useful for discovering disease associations or identifying tissues with similar cell states.
Sources: [src/scimilarity/cell_query.py](src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L206-L252), [src/scimilarity/cell_query.py](src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L150-L178)

### Advanced Search Options

SCimilarity provides multiple search strategies depending on your needs:

| Method | Use Case | Speed | Precision | Resources |
|--------|----------|-------|-----------|-----------|
| `search_nearest` | Standard k-NN search | ⚡ Fast | High | Moderate RAM |
| `search_exhaustive` | Find all cells within distance threshold | 🐢 Slow | Complete | High RAM |
| `search_centroid_nearest` | Search from cluster centroids | ⚡⚡ Fastest | Moderate | Low RAM |
| `search_cluster_centroids_nearest` | Batch search for multiple clusters | ⚡ Fast | High | Moderate RAM |

> [!TIP]
> For most use cases, `search_nearest` with `k=1000` provides an excellent balance of comprehensiveness and performance. Only switch to exhaustive search when you need guaranteed completeness within a specific distance threshold.

For detailed API reference and parameter explanations, see [Cell Query API Reference](9-cell-query-api-reference) and [K-NN Search with HNSW](10-k-nn-search-with-hnsw). Advanced filtering options are covered in [Metadata Filtering and Query Optimization](12-metadata-filtering-and-query-optimization).

## Workflow 2: Cell Annotation (Classifying Cell Types)

SCimilarity can automatically annotate cell types by comparing your cells to a reference database of annotated cells. This is particularly valuable for exploring new datasets or validating existing annotations.

![Cell Annotation Workflow](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/annotation_thumbnail.png?raw=true)

### Quick Example: Annotate Unknown Cell Types

```python
from scimilarity import CellAnnotation

# Initialize CellAnnotation
model_path = "/models/model_v1.1"
ca = CellAnnotation(model_path=model_path)

# Preprocess your data
adata = align_dataset(adata, ca.gene_order)
adata = lognorm_counts(adata)

# Annotate the entire dataset
annotated_adata = ca.annotate_dataset(adata)

# View predictions
print(annotated_adata.obs["scimilarity_prediction"].value_counts())
```

The `annotate_dataset` method performs three operations in one call:
1. **Generates embeddings** for your cells using the pre-trained encoder
2. **Searches k-NN** to find similar annotated cells in the reference database
3. **Predicts cell types** based on neighbor labels using weighted voting

### Understanding Predictions

The annotation process adds several columns to your AnnData object:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `scimilarity_prediction` | Predicted cell type label |
| `scimilarity_confidence` | Prediction confidence score (0-1) |
| `scimilarity_votes` | Vote distribution across candidate cell types |

By default, predictions are made from the 50 nearest neighbors. You can customize this behavior:

```python
# Get detailed prediction information
preds, confidences, votes, neighbor_metadata = ca.get_predictions_knn(
    embeddings=adata.X,
    k=50,  # Use 50 nearest neighbors
    weighting=True,  # Apply distance-based weighting
)
```

The `weighting` parameter applies exponential decay to neighbor votes based on distance, giving more weight to closer cells.
Sources: [src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py](src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L148-L237), [src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py](src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L281-L300)

### Safelist and Blocklist Cell Types

You can constrain predictions to specific cell types or exclude unwanted categories:

```python
# Only predict from specific cell types
ca.safelist_celltypes(["T cell", "B cell", "NK cell"])

# Exclude specific cell types from predictions
ca.blocklist_celltypes(["Unknown", "Low quality"])

# Reset to use all available cell types
ca.reset_knn()
```

These methods modify the k-NN index in-place by marking cell types as deleted, allowing you to iteratively refine your annotation strategy.
Sources: [src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py](src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L92-L116), [src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py](src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L118-L146)

For complete annotation API reference, see [Cell Annotation API Reference](13-cell-annotation-api-reference). To understand the classification methodology in detail, visit [Understanding Cell Type Classification](14-understanding-cell-type-classification).

## Workflow 3: Gene Attribution (Understanding Cell Differences)

The Interpreter module helps you understand the genetic drivers that distinguish two cell states by computing feature attributions using integrated gradients.

![Gene Attribution](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/advanced_thumbnail.png?raw=true)

### Quick Example: Identify Genes Differentiating Two Cell Types

```python
from scimilarity import CellEmbedding
from scimilarity.interpreter import Interpreter

# Initialize embedding model
ce = CellEmbedding(model_path="/models/model_v1.1")

# Initialize interpreter with the encoder
interpreter = Interpreter(ce.model, ce.gene_order)

# Select anchor and negative cells
# (anchor: cell state of interest, negative: comparison cell state)
anchor_cell = adata[adata.obs["cell_type"] == "Myofibroblast"].X[0]
negative_cell = adata[adata.obs["cell_type"] == "Fibroblast"].X[0]

# Compute attributions
attrs = interpreter.get_attributions(
    anchors=anchor_cell,
    negatives=negative_cell
)

# Get ranked gene list
genes_df = interpreter.get_ranked_genes(attrs)
print(genes_df.head())
```

The attribution scores indicate which genes contribute most to the difference between the two cell states in the latent space.

### Visualizing Gene Contributions

```python
# Plot top contributing genes
interpreter.plot_ranked_genes(
    attrs_df=genes_df,
    n_plot=15,
    filename="gene_attributions.png"
)
```

This visualization shows the genes with the highest attribution scores, helping you quickly identify key molecular drivers of phenotypic differences.
Sources: [src/scimilarity/interpreter.py](src/scimilarity/interpreter.py#L69-L132), [src/scimilarity/interpreter.py](src/scimilarity/interpreter.py#L133-L164)

For detailed methodology on how attributions are computed, see [Gene Attribution and Comparison](27-gene-attribution-and-comparison). Complete API reference is available at [Interpreter API Reference](28-interpreter-api-reference).

## Summary: Choosing Your Workflow

SCimilarity's three primary workflows address different research questions:

| Research Question | Recommended Workflow | Primary API |
|-------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| "Which studies/diseases have cells like mine?" | Cell Search | `CellQuery` |
| "What are these cells' types?" | Cell Annotation | `CellAnnotation` |
| "Which genes drive the difference between these cells?" | Gene Attribution | `Interpreter` |

All three workflows share the same preprocessing pipeline (`align_dataset` → `lognorm_counts`), making it easy to transition between analyses. The APIs are designed to work independently or in combination—for example, you might first search for similar cells, then annotate your results, and finally use the interpreter to understand the molecular differences.

# Installation and Setup



This guide provides comprehensive instructions for installing and configuring SCimilarity across different environments. SCimilarity is a single cell embedding framework that quantifies similarity between expression states, enabling large-scale cell search capabilities across millions of profiles. Whether you're setting up for local development, production deployment, or interactive analysis, this document covers all installation pathways and their requirements.

## System Requirements

Before installing SCimilarity, ensure your system meets the hardware and software prerequisites for your intended use case. The requirements vary significantly based on whether you plan to perform cell queries, model training, or both.

**Hardware Requirements:**

| Use Case | Minimum RAM | Recommended RAM | GPU | Storage |
|----------|-------------|-----------------|-----|---------|
| Cell Queries | 64 GB | 128 GB+ | Optional | 50 GB+ |
| Model Training | 128 GB | 256 GB+ | Required (NVIDIA) | 100 GB+ |
| Development | 32 GB | 64 GB | Optional | 20 GB+ |

**Software Requirements:**

- Python 3.10 or higher
- Operating System: Linux (recommended) or macOS
- Package Manager: pip, conda, or Docker
- Git (for development installation)

> [!TIP]
> SCimilarity has very high memory requirements due to its ability to perform rapid searches across tens of millions of cells. If loading the model or making kNN queries crashes despite sufficient memory, ensure you're using recent versions of dependencies like `hnswlib` and `numpy`. The Docker container or Conda environment below include tested dependency versions.
> Sources: [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L27-L35)

## Installation Overview

The installation architecture supports multiple deployment pathways depending on your environment and needs:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Installation Decision] --> B{Installation Type}
    B --> C[Stable Release]
    B --> D[Development Version]
    B --> E[Conda Environment]
    B --> F[Docker Container]
    
    C --> G[pip install scimilarity]
    D --> H[git clone + pip install -e]
    E --> I[Conda env + pip install]
    F --> J[Docker pull + volume bind]
    
    G --> K[Download Models from Zenodo]
    H --> K
    I --> K
    J --> K
    
    K --> L[Configuration Complete]
    
    style C fill:#e1f5ff
    style E fill:#e1f5ff
    style F fill:#e1f5ff
```

## Installation Methods

### Method 1: Stable Release via pip

The simplest installation method uses pip to install the latest stable release from PyPI. This approach is recommended for most users who want to quickly get started with production-ready code.

```bash
pip install scimilarity
```

This command downloads and installs all core dependencies automatically, including PyTorch, scanpy, tiledb-vector-search, and other required packages [setup.cfg](setup.cfg#L63-L76). The stable release includes all bug fixes and features from the latest version (currently 0.4.1) [setup.cfg](setup.cfg#L18).

### Method 2: Development Version from GitHub

For users who need the latest features or plan to contribute to SCimilarity, install directly from the GitHub repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/genentech/scimilarity.git
cd scimilarity
pip install -e .
```

The `-e` flag creates an editable installation, allowing you to modify the source code and have changes reflected immediately without reinstalling [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L14-L18). This method is ideal for developers and researchers who want to experiment with cutting-edge features or extend the library.

### Method 3: Conda Environment Setup

For reproducible environments and better dependency management, we recommend using Conda. This approach provides isolated environments with consistent dependency versions across different systems.

**Step 1: Create the Conda environment** using the provided environment specification:

```bash
conda env create -f docs/_static/environment.yaml
conda activate scimilarity
```

**Step 2: Install SCimilarity** within the activated environment:

```bash
pip install scimilarity
```

The Conda environment file [docs/_static/environment.yaml](docs/_static/environment.yaml#L1-L13) includes:

| Package | Version | Purpose |
|---------|---------|---------|
| Python | 3.10 | Core runtime |
| ipykernel | Latest | Jupyter kernel |
| ipython | Latest | Enhanced Python shell |
| ipywidgets | Latest | Interactive widgets |
| leidenalg | Latest | Community detection |
| pip | Latest | Package manager |

This configuration includes essential channels (nvidia, pytorch, bioconda, conda-forge) for optimized package access [docs/_static/environment.yaml](docs/_static/environment.yaml#L3-L5).

### Method 4: Docker Container

Docker provides the most consistent installation experience across different platforms by containerizing the entire environment including all dependencies and system libraries.

**Pull the Docker image:**

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/genentech/scimilarity:latest
```

The Docker image is built on Fedora 42 and includes all required system packages, Python libraries, and scientific computing tools [docker/Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L98).

**Container Bind Points:**

The Docker container includes four predefined volume bind points for organizing your data and models:

| Bind Point | Purpose | Required |
|------------|---------|----------|
| `/models` | SCimilarity model files | Yes |
| `/data` | scRNA-seq data repository | Yes |
| `/workspace` | Notebook and workspace directory | Yes |
| `/scratch` | Temporary files | Optional |

**Launch Jupyter Notebook:**

```bash
docker run -it --platform linux/amd64 -p 8888:8888 \
    -v /path/to/workspace:/workspace \
    -v /path/to/data:/data \
    -v /path/to/models:/models \
    ghcr.io/genentech/scimilarity:latest start-notebook
```

This command starts a Jupyter Notebook server accessible at `http://localhost:8888`, with your workspace, data, and models mounted as volumes [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L82-L91). The `start-notebook.sh` script launches the notebook server in the container's `/workspace` directory [docker/start-notebook.sh](docker/start-notebook.sh#L1-L4).

> [!TIP]
> Models are not included in the Docker container to reduce image size and allow version flexibility. You must download pretrained models separately from Zenodo and bind them to the `/models` volume.
> Sources: [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L72-L73)
> </cgq_tip>
>

>
> **Available Resources:**
>
> | Resource | Description | Size |
> |----------|-------------|------|
> | Pretrained encoder | Trained model weights for cell embeddings | ~500 MB |
> | Cell embeddings | Pre-computed embeddings for reference datasets | 10-50 GB |
> | kNN graphs | Pre-built neighbor graphs for fast searching | 5-20 GB |
> | Metadata | Cell type annotations and metadata | 1-5 GB |
>
> <CgxTip>
> Download only the resources you need. The pretrained encoder is sufficient for most use cases, while embeddings and kNN graphs provide instant search capabilities without recomputation.
> Sources: [README.rst](README.rst#L29-L32)

## Verification

After installation, verify your setup by testing core functionality:

```python
import scimilarity
import torch

# Check version
print(f"SCimilarity version: {scimilarity.__version__}")

# Check PyTorch availability
print(f"PyTorch available: {torch.cuda.is_available()}")

# Import key modules
from scimilarity import CellEmbedding, CellQuery, CellAnnotation
print("All modules imported successfully!")
```

Successful verification confirms that:
- SCimilarity is installed correctly
- All dependencies are compatible
- PyTorch recognizes your GPU (if available)

## Troubleshooting

**Memory Issues:**
- **Problem**: kNN queries crash with out-of-memory errors
- **Solution**: Ensure at least 64 GB RAM available. Check `hnswlib` and `numpy` versions are recent [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L31-L35)

**Import Errors:**
- **Problem**: `ModuleNotFoundError` for dependencies
- **Solution**: Use the Conda environment or Docker container for tested dependency combinations

**Docker Platform Issues:**
- **Problem**: Container fails to start on ARM-based Macs
- **Solution**: Use `--platform linux/amd64` flag in docker run command [docs/install.rst](docs/install.rst#L83)

**GPU Recognition:**
- **Problem**: PyTorch doesn't detect GPU
- **Solution**: Install CUDA-enabled PyTorch version or use Conda with nvidia channel [docs/_static/environment.yaml](docs/_static/environment.yaml#L4)

- **[Docker Usage](5-docker-usage)** - Advanced Docker configuration for production deployments

# Downloading Pretrained Models and Data



This guide walks you through acquiring the essential pretrained models and data needed to use SCimilarity's powerful cell search and annotation capabilities. The pretrained model enables you to leverage a foundation model trained on millions of single-cell expression profiles, allowing immediate use without requiring extensive computational resources or training time.

Sources: [README.rst](README.rst#L1-L43)

## Understanding What You Need to Download

SCimilarity requires two main components to function: the pretrained model files and your query datasets. The pretrained model includes neural network weights, gene ordering information, and pre-built kNN indices that enable rapid similarity search across millions of cells. Additionally, tutorial datasets are available to help you get started with hands-on examples.

![SCimilarity Workflow](https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/blob/main/docs/_static/search_thumbnail_1.png?raw=true)

The architecture follows a clear separation of concerns: the model provides the embedding and search infrastructure, while your data represents the query states you want to investigate. When you download the pretrained model package, you receive everything needed for inference, including the encoder architecture weights and supporting metadata files.

Sources: [cell_embedding.py](src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py#L1-L80), [nn_models.py](src/scimilarity/nn_models.py#L82-L100)

## Downloading the Pretrained Model

The SCimilarity pretrained model v1.1 is hosted on Zenodo and contains all necessary components for cell embedding, similarity search, and annotation. Use the following commands to download and extract the model:

```bash
# Download the model tarball
curl -L -o /models/model_v1.1.tar.gz \
  https://zenodo.org/records/10685499/files/model_v1.1.tar.gz?download=1

# Extract the archive
tar -xzvf /models/model_v1.1.tar.gz
```

This is a large file (several gigabytes), so download and extraction may take several minutes depending on your internet connection and disk speed. Ensure you have at least 10GB of free disk space available.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Zenodo Repository] --> B[Download model_v1.1.tar.gz]
    B --> C[Extract to /models/model_v1.1]
    C --> D[Verify Required Files]
    D --> E[Ready for Use]
    
    style A fill:#e3f2fd
    style B fill:#bbdefb
    style C fill:#90caf9
    style D fill:#64b5f6
    style E fill:#2196f3
```

> [!TIP]
> Choose a location with sufficient disk space and fast I/O performance, such as an SSD, as the kNN index will be frequently accessed during queries. The model files should remain uncompressed for optimal performance.

Sources: [cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb](docs/notebooks/cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb#L20-L30)

## Model File Structure

After extraction, the model directory contains several critical files that the SCimilarity API expects to find. Understanding this structure helps troubleshoot setup issues:

| File | Purpose | Required By |
|------|---------|-------------|
| `encoder.ckpt` | Neural network weights | CellEmbedding, CellQuery, CellAnnotation |
| `gene_order.tsv` | Canonical gene ordering | CellEmbedding |
| `layer_sizes.json` | Network architecture dimensions | CellEmbedding |
| `label_ints.csv` | Cell type label mappings | CellAnnotation |
| `cell_embedding` | Pre-computed embeddings (TileDB) | CellQuery |
| `cell_metadata` | Cell metadata database (TileDB) | CellQuery |
| `knn_index` | HNSW kNN search index | CellQuery, CellSearchKNN |

```
/models/model_v1.1/
├── encoder.ckpt              # PyTorch model weights
├── gene_order.tsv            # Gene identifiers
├── layer_sizes.json          # Network dimensions
├── label_ints.csv            # Cell type mappings
├── cell_embedding/           # TileDB array with embeddings
├── cell_metadata/            # TileDB array with metadata
└── knn_index                 # HNSW index file
```

When you initialize a CellQuery or CellAnnotation object, it automatically looks for these files in the specified model directory [cell_embedding.py](src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py#L24-L48). The gene order file is particularly important—it defines the canonical gene ordering that your query data must match for accurate embeddings.

Sources: [cell_embedding.py](src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py#L31-L48), [cell_search_knn.py](src/scimilarity/cell_search_knn.py#L40-L63)

## Downloading Tutorial Datasets

To follow along with the SCimilarity tutorials and verify your installation, download the provided tutorial datasets. These are smaller, curated datasets that demonstrate various capabilities:

```bash
# Download the cell search tutorial dataset
curl -L -o '/data/GSE136831_subsample.h5ad' \
  https://zenodo.org/records/13685881/files/GSE136831_subsample.h5ad?download=1
```

Additional tutorial datasets are available for different use cases:
- **Cell Search Tutorial**: IPF lung fibroblast data from Adams et al. 2020
- **Cell Annotation Tutorial**: Annotated datasets for classification tasks
- **Training Tutorial**: Sample data for training custom models

These datasets are in AnnData format (.h5ad files), which is the standard format for single-cell analysis in Python. The tutorial notebooks provide complete examples of how to load, process, and query these datasets.

Sources: [cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb](docs/notebooks/cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb#L1-L45)

## System Requirements and Memory Considerations

Running SCimilarity with the pretrained model demands substantial system resources due to the scale of the precomputed embeddings and kNN indices:

| Component | Minimum Requirement | Recommended |
|-----------|---------------------|-------------|
| System RAM | 64 GB | 128 GB+ |
| Disk Space | 20 GB | SSD with fast I/O |
| CPU | Multi-core | 8+ cores |
| GPU | Not required | Optional for training |

> [!TIP]
> If you experience crashes during model loading or kNN queries, verify your dependency versions. Older versions of hnswlib or numpy can cause memory issues. Consider using the provided Docker container or Conda environment file for a stable setup.

The memory requirements stem from loading the entire kNN index into memory for fast similarity search. The index enables queries across 23.4 million cells in seconds, but this speed comes at the cost of significant RAM usage. For environments with limited memory, consider using TileDB vector search which can operate with lower memory requirements at the cost of slower query performance.

Sources: [install.rst](docs/install.rst#L30-L40), [cell_search_knn.py](src/scimilarity/cell_search_knn.py#L40-L63)

## Verifying Your Downloaded Model

After downloading and extracting the model, verify that all required files are present and accessible:

```python
import os
from scimilarity import CellQuery

# Check model directory contents
model_path = "/models/model_v1.1"
expected_files = [
    "encoder.ckpt",
    "gene_order.tsv", 
    "layer_sizes.json",
    "label_ints.csv"
]

print("Verifying model files...")
for filename in expected_files:
    filepath = os.path.join(model_path, filename)
    exists = "✓" if os.path.exists(filepath) else "✗"
    print(f"  {exists} {filename}")

# Try initializing CellQuery to validate integrity
try:
    cq = CellQuery(model_path=model_path)
    print("\n✓ Model loaded successfully!")
    print(f"  Latent dimension: {cq.latent_dim}")
    print(f"  Number of genes: {cq.n_genes}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"\n✗ Error loading model: {e}")
```

This verification script checks for essential files and attempts to initialize the CellQuery class, which performs additional validation such as checking the gene order file format and loading the encoder weights. If successful, it will display the model's latent dimension and gene count.

Sources: [cell_embedding.py](src/scimilarity/cell_embedding.py#L19-L70), [cell_query.py](src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L31-L92)

## Using Downloaded Models with Docker

The SCimilarity Docker container provides a pre-configured environment but requires you to mount your downloaded model and data directories. The container includes four preset bind points for easy integration:

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/genentech/scimilarity:latest

docker run -it --platform linux/amd64 -p 8888:8888 \
    -v /path/to/workspace:/workspace \
    -v /path/to/data:/data \
    -v /path/to/models:/models \
    ghcr.io/genentech/scimilarity:latest start-notebook
```

| Bind Point | Purpose | Local Path Example |
|------------|---------|-------------------|
| `/models` | Pretrained model files | `/local/scimilarity/models` |
| `/data` | scRNA-seq datasets | `/local/scimilarity/data` |
| `/workspace` | Notebooks and scripts | `/local/scimilarity/workspace` |
| `/scratch` | Temporary files | `/tmp/scimilarity` |

The Docker approach ensures all dependencies are correctly configured, including versions of hnswlib, numpy, and PyTorch that are known to work well with SCimilarity. This eliminates the common issue of crashes due to incompatible library versions.

Sources: [install.rst](docs/install.rst#L60-L99), [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L50)

## Setting Up a Conda Environment

For users preferring a Conda-based setup, SCimilarity provides an environment configuration file that specifies compatible package versions:

```bash
# Download the environment file
wget https://github.com/Genentech/scimilarity/raw/main/docs/_static/environment.yaml

# Create the Conda environment
conda env create -f environment.yaml

# Activate the environment
conda activate scimilarity

# Install the SCimilarity package
pip install scimilarity
```

The environment file includes precise version specifications for critical dependencies like PyTorch, hnswlib, and numpy, preventing compatibility issues that can arise from version mismatches. After activating the environment, you can proceed with downloading the model and data as described above.

Sources: [install.rst](docs/install.rst#L42-L58), [environment.yaml](docs/_static/environment.yaml#L1-L30)

## Integration with SCimilarity APIs

Once downloaded, the pretrained model integrates seamlessly with SCimilarity's main APIs through simple initialization:

```python
from scimilarity import CellQuery, CellAnnotation

# Initialize for cell search queries
model_path = "/models/model_v1.1"
cq = CellQuery(model_path=model_path)

# Initialize for cell type annotation
ca = CellAnnotation(model_path=model_path)

# The model is now ready for queries
embeddings = cq.get_embeddings(your_data_matrix)
nearest = cq.search_nearest(embeddings, k=100)
```

The initialization process automatically loads the encoder weights, reads the gene order file, and prepares the kNN index for fast similarity search. For CellAnnotation, additional label mappings are loaded to enable cell type classification. Both classes inherit from CellEmbedding, which handles the core model loading logic.

Sources: [cell_query.py](src/scimilarity/cell_query.py#L31-L92), [cell_annotation.py](src/scimilarity/cell_annotation.py#L23-L70)

## Troubleshooting Common Issues

| Issue | Symptoms | Solution |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Model not found | FileNotFoundError for encoder.ckpt | Verify extraction completed without errors |
| Gene mismatch | Shape errors during embedding | Use `align_dataset` to match gene order |
| Memory crashes | Process killed during kNN load | Increase RAM or reduce memory_budget parameter |
| Slow queries | Queries taking minutes instead of seconds | Use HNSW index instead of exhaustive search |
| Import errors | Missing dependency errors | Use Docker or Conda environment file |

The most common issue is gene order mismatch between your query data and the pretrained model's expected gene order. The `align_dataset` utility function handles this by reordering and filtering your data to match the model's canonical gene list:

```python
from scimilarity.utils import align_dataset

# Your data may have different genes
aligned_data = align_dataset(
    data=your_anndata,
    target_gene_order=cq.gene_order,
    keep_obsm=True
)
```

Sources: [utils.py](src/scimilarity/utils.py#L50-L134), [cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb](docs/notebooks/cell_search_tutorial_1.ipynb#L50-L120)

## Next Steps

After successfully downloading and verifying the pretrained model, you're ready to explore SCimilarity's capabilities:

- [Quick Start](2-quick-start) - Begin with a hands-on tutorial showing basic cell search functionality
- [Docker Usage](5-docker-usage) - Learn advanced Docker configurations and deployment strategies  
- [Cell Embedding Fundamentals](6-cell-embedding-fundamentals) - Understand how gene expression is transformed into latent representations
- [Cell Query API Reference](9-cell-query-api-reference) - Detailed documentation of query methods and parameters

The pretrained model provides immediate access to SCimilarity's foundation model capabilities, enabling you to search across millions of annotated cells and perform cell type annotation without any training. Download the tutorial datasets and work through the notebooks to build familiarity with the API before applying SCimilarity to your own research questions.


# Docker Usage



Docker provides a complete, isolated environment for running SCimilarity with all dependencies pre-configured. This approach eliminates local installation conflicts and ensures reproducibility across different development machines. The Docker setup is particularly valuable for computational biology workflows where consistent environments are critical for reproducible research.

## Docker Architecture Overview

The SCimilarity Docker container creates a self-contained computational environment with Fedora Linux as the base operating system. The architecture follows a layered approach where system dependencies, Python packages, and the SCimilarity library are installed in sequence, creating a fully functional data science workspace.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Host System"
        A[Your Machine] -->|Mount| B[/data/]
        A -->|Mount| C[/models/]
        A -->|Mount| D[/workspace/]
        A -->|Mount| E[/scratch/]
    end
    
    subgraph "Docker Container"
        F[Fedora 42 Base]
        F --> G[System Packages<br/>Python 3, GCC, CMake]
        G --> H[Scientific Libraries<br/>NumPy, SciPy, Pandas]
        H --> I[ML/AI Frameworks<br/>PyTorch, scikit-learn]
        I --> J[Bioinformatics Tools<br/>Scanpy, AnnData]
        J --> K[SCimilarity Library<br/>Installed from GitHub]
        K --> L[Jupyter Notebook Server]
    end
    
    B -.->|SCDATA_HOME| L
    C -.->|SCMODEL_HOME| L
    D -.->|Notebook Directory| L
    E -.->|Temporary Storage| L
    
    style F fill:#e1f5ff
    style L fill:#ffe1e1
```

This architecture separates persistent data storage from the container's ephemeral file system through volume mounts. The container runs Jupyter Notebook as the primary interface, exposing it on port 8888 for web-based interaction with SCimilarity's capabilities.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L98), [start-notebook.sh](docker/start-notebook.sh#L1-L4)

## Building the Docker Image

The Docker image builds automatically from the included Dockerfile, installing all required dependencies and the SCimilarity library itself. The build process downloads and configures approximately 80+ packages spanning system utilities, scientific computing libraries, and machine learning frameworks.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Start Build] --> B[Pull Fedora 42 Base]
    B --> C[Install System Packages<br/>via DNF]
    C --> D[Install Python Dependencies<br/>via pip3]
    D --> E[Clone SCimilarity Repo]
    E --> F[Install SCimilarity<br/>pip install .]
    F --> G[Copy Notebook Script]
    G --> H[Configure Volumes<br/>data, models, workspace, scratch]
    H --> I[Set Environment Variables<br/>SCDATA_HOME, SCMODEL_HOME]
    I --> J[Complete Image]
    
    style C fill:#fff4e1
    style D fill:#fff4e1
    style J fill:#e1ffe1
```

To build the image, navigate to the repository root and execute:

```bash
docker build -t scimilarity:latest ./docker
```

This command compiles all layers into a single image tagged as `scimilarity:latest`. The build process may take 10-20 minutes depending on your network speed, as it downloads numerous scientific packages. The image size will be substantial (several GB) due to the inclusion of PyTorch, scientific computing stacks, and bioinformatics tools.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L98)

## Running the Container

Once built, run the container with appropriate volume mounts to access your local data and models. The container exposes Jupyter Notebook on port 8888, which you can access through your web browser.

### Basic Execution

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name scimilarity \
  -p 8888:8888 \
  -v $(pwd)/data:/data \
  -v $(pwd)/models:/models \
  -v $(pwd)/workspace:/workspace \
  -v $(pwd)/scratch:/scratch \
  scimilarity:latest
```

### Volume Mount Strategy

The container uses four volume mounts to separate different types of data:

| Volume Mount | Purpose | Environment Variable | Recommended Local Path |
|-------------|---------|----------------------|------------------------|
| `/data` | Input datasets (AnnData, Zarr, TileDB) | `SCDATA_HOME` | `./data` |
| `/models` | Pretrained model files | `SCMODEL_HOME` | `./models` |
| `/workspace` | Jupyter notebooks and analysis scripts | — | `./workspace` |
| `/scratch` | Temporary files and intermediate results | — | `./scratch` |

This separation ensures that your data persists outside the container, allowing you to upgrade or rebuild the Docker image without losing your work. The `/workspace` directory serves as the default notebook directory, where you should place your analysis notebooks.

> [!TIP]
> Always use absolute paths or expand `$PWD` when mounting volumes to avoid path resolution issues. Relative paths can behave unexpectedly depending on your Docker Compose version or Docker Desktop configuration.

### Accessing Jupyter Notebook

After starting the container, access Jupyter Notebook at `http://localhost:8888`. The container runs Jupyter without authentication in the default configuration, making it suitable for local development environments. For production deployments, consider adding security measures such as password authentication or SSL/TLS encryption.

The notebook server automatically starts in the `/workspace` directory, so any notebooks you create or modify there will persist on your host machine through the volume mount.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L6-L18), [start-notebook.sh](docker/start-notebook.sh#L1-L4)

## Installed Dependencies

The Docker image includes a comprehensive scientific computing stack optimized for single-cell analysis and machine learning. Understanding these dependencies helps troubleshoot issues and extend functionality.

### System-Level Dependencies

Fedora packages provide the foundational tools including compilers, scientific libraries, and utilities:

| Category | Key Packages | Purpose |
|----------|--------------|---------|
| Build Tools | gcc-c++, cmake, Cython | Compilation of Python extensions |
| Data I/O | bzip2, lz4, zstd | Compression and archive handling |
| Scientific Computing | python3-numpy, python3-scipy, python3-pandas | Numerical computing foundation |
| Visualization | python3-matplotlib, python3-seaborn | Plotting and statistical graphics |
| Documentation | pandoc, nbsphinx, python3-pydata-sphinx-theme | Documentation generation |
| Network Tools | python3-aiohttp, python3-cloudpickle | Asynchronous I/O and serialization |

### Python Package Dependencies

PyPI packages provide domain-specific functionality for single-cell genomics and machine learning:

| Domain | Packages | Functionality |
|--------|----------|---------------|
| Deep Learning | torch, pytorch-lightning, captum | Neural networks and attribution |
| Single-Cell Analysis | scanpy, scrublet | Preprocessing and doublet detection |
| Clustering | leidenalg, louvain, python3-igraph | Community detection algorithms |
| Dimensionality Reduction | umap-learn, hnswlib | Manifold learning and ANN search |
| Data Storage | tiledb, tiledb-cloud, python3-zarr, python3-h5py | Multi-format data handling |
| Bioinformatics | python3-biopython, obonet | Biological data and ontologies |
| Visualization | circlize, python3-matplotlib-scalebar | Circular plots and scale bars |

This comprehensive dependency set enables SCimilarity's full functionality without requiring any additional package installation within the container.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L20-L94)

## Configuration and Customization

The Docker environment can be customized through environment variables and modifications to the startup script.

### Environment Variables

Two critical environment variables configure data paths within the container:

| Variable | Default Value | Purpose |
|----------|---------------|---------|
| `SCDATA_HOME` | `/data` | Root directory for input datasets |
| `SCMODEL_HOME` | `/models` | Root directory for pretrained models |

These variables are set in the Dockerfile but can be overridden at runtime using the `-e` flag:

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name scimilarity \
  -p 8888:8888 \
  -e SCDATA_HOME=/custom/data \
  -e SCMODEL_HOME=/custom/models \
  -v $(pwd)/data:/custom/data \
  -v $(pwd)/models:/custom/models \
  scimilarity:latest
```

### Custom Startup Commands

While the default entry point launches Jupyter Notebook, you can override this to run scripts directly or execute specific commands:

```bash
# Run an interactive shell
docker run -it scimilarity:latest /bin/bash

# Execute a Python script
docker run -v $(pwd)/scripts:/scripts scimilarity:latest python /scripts/my_analysis.py

# Launch Jupyter Lab instead of Notebook
docker run -d -p 8888:8888 scimilarity:latest jupyter lab --ip=0.0.0.0 --no-browser
```

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L16-L18), [start-notebook.sh](docker/start-notebook.sh#L1-L4)

## GPU Support

The base Dockerfile does not include NVIDIA CUDA support by default. For GPU-accelerated model training and inference, modify the Dockerfile to use an NVIDIA base image and install CUDA-enabled PyTorch:

1. Change the base image from `fedora:42` to `nvidia/cuda:11.8.0-devel-fedora42`
2. Install PyTorch with CUDA support: `pip3 install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118`
3. Run containers with GPU access: `docker run --gpus all -d scimilarity-gpu:latest`

GPU acceleration significantly speeds up neural network training and large-scale embedding computations, particularly when working with datasets containing millions of cells.

> [!TIP]
> When adding GPU support, verify that your host system has compatible NVIDIA drivers and the nvidia-container-toolkit installed. Without proper host configuration, GPU passthrough will fail silently, and PyTorch will fall back to CPU operations.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L94)

## Common Troubleshooting

### Port Conflicts

If port 8888 is already in use on your host system, map the container to a different port:

```bash
docker run -d -p 9999:8888 scimilarity:latest
```

Then access Jupyter at `http://localhost:9999` instead.

### Permission Issues

Volume mounts may encounter permission problems if the container runs as a different user than the host. Resolve this by matching user IDs:

```bash
docker run -d \
  --user $(id -u):$(id -g) \
  -v $(pwd)/workspace:/workspace \
  scimilarity:latest
```

### Memory Constraints

Large-scale single-cell analyses can be memory-intensive. Increase Docker's allocated memory through Docker Desktop settings or use the `--memory` flag:

```bash
docker run -d --memory=16g scimilarity:latest
```

### Build Failures

If package installations fail during the build, try these strategies:

1. Clear Docker's build cache: `docker build --no-cache -t scimilarity:latest ./docker`
2. Use a different mirror or proxy if network issues occur
3. Check the Fedora 42 package repository availability for your region

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L98)

## Production Considerations

While the default Docker configuration serves development well, production deployments require additional security measures:

1. **Authentication**: Replace the default Jupyter configuration with password or token-based authentication
2. **Network Security**: Use Docker networks or Kubernetes network policies to restrict container access
3. **Resource Limits**: Implement CPU and memory quotas to prevent runaway processes
4. **Health Checks**: Add container health checks to monitor Jupyter Notebook status
5. **Logging**: Configure log drivers to centralize container logs for monitoring and debugging

For scalable deployments serving multiple users, consider using JupyterHub with DockerSpawner to manage user containers dynamically.

**Sources:** [Dockerfile](docker/Dockerfile#L1-L98), [start-notebook.sh](docker/start-notebook.sh#L1-L4)
